content: 1. Chlorthalidone is a yellowish-white powder with a molecular weight of 338.76. It is practically insoluble in water, ether, and chloroform, but it is soluble in methanol and slightly soluble in ethanol. 2. 3. Azilsartan inhibits the pressor effects of angiotensin II infusion in a dose-dependent manner. A single dose of azilsartan equivalent to 32 mg of azilsartan medoxomil inhibited the maximal pressor effect by approximately 90% at peak and about 60% at 24 hours. 4. Following single and repeated administration of azilsartan medoxomil to healthy subjects, plasma concentrations of angiotensin I and II and plasma renin activity increased, while plasma aldosterone concentrations decreased. No clinically significant effects on serum potassium or sodium levels were observed. 5. The diuretic effect of chlorthalidone begins approximately 2 to 6 hours after administration and lasts for up to 72 hours. 6. After oral administration of Edarbyclor, peak plasma concentrations of azilsartan and chlorthalidone are reached at approximately 3 hours and 1 hour, respectively. 7. The rate (Cmax and Tmax) and extent (AUC) of absorption of azilsartan are similar whether it is administered alone or with chlorthalidone. However, the Cmax of chlorthalidone from Edarbyclor was 47% higher compared to chlorthalidone alone. 8. The elimination half-lives of azilsartan and chlorthalidone are approximately 12 hours and 45 hours, respectively. 9. Food does not have a clinically significant effect on the bioavailability of Edarbyclor. 10. Azilsartan medoxomil is rapidly hydrolyzed to azilsartan, its active metabolite, in the gastrointestinal tract during absorption. Azilsartan medoxomil is not detected in plasma after oral administration. 11. The estimated absolute bioavailability of azilsartan following administration of azilsartan medoxomil is approximately 60%. 12. After oral administration of azilsartan medoxomil, peak plasma concentrations (Cmax) of azilsartan are reached within 1.5 to 3 hours. Food does not affect the bioavailability of azilsartan. 13. The volume of distribution of azilsartan is approximately 16 liters. Azilsartan is highly bound to human plasma proteins (>99%), primarily serum albumin. Protein binding remains constant at plasma concentrations well above those achieved with recommended doses. 14. In animal studies, minimal azilsartan-associated radioactivity crossed the blood-brain barrier. Azilsartan crossed the placental barrier in pregnant rats and was distributed to the fetus. 15. In whole blood, chlorthalidone predominantly binds to erythrocyte carbonic anhydrase. In plasma, approximately 75% of chlorthalidone is bound to plasma proteins, with 58% bound to albumin. 16. Azilsartan is metabolized into two primary metabolites. The major metabolite in plasma, referred to as M-II, is formed by O-dealkylation, while the minor metabolite, M-I, is formed by decarboxylation. Neither M-I nor M-II contributes to the pharmacologic activity of azilsartan medoxomil. 17. The major enzyme responsible for azilsartan metabolism is CYP2C9. Following an oral dose of 14C-labeled azilsartan medoxomil, approximately 55% of radioactivity was recovered in feces and 42% in urine, with 15% of the dose excreted in urine as azilsartan. 18. The elimination half-life of azilsartan is approximately 11 hours, and its renal clearance is about 2.3 mL/min. Steady-state levels of azilsartan are achieved within 5 days, with no accumulation in plasma observed with repeated once-daily dosing. 19. The majority of chlorthalidone is excreted unchanged by the kidneys. Nonrenal routes of elimination have not been clarified. Data on the percentage of dose excreted as unchanged drug and metabolites, drug concentrations in body fluids, organ uptake, fetal distribution, or passage across the blood-brain barrier are not available. 20. The pharmacokinetics of azilsartan were studied in single and multiple-dose studies to assess the effects of demographic and functional factors. 21. No carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or fertility studies have been conducted with the combination of azilsartan medoxomil and chlorthalidone. However, such studies have been conducted for azilsartan medoxomil alone. 22. Azilsartan medoxomil was not carcinogenic in 26-week transgenic (Tg.rasH2) mouse studies or 2-year rat studies. 23. M-II was not carcinogenic in similar studies. 24. Azilsartan medoxomil, azilsartan, and M-II were positive for structural aberrations in the Chinese Hamster Lung Cytogenic Assay. Structural chromosomal aberrations were observed with azilsartan medoxomil without metabolic activation. Azilsartan and M-II were also positive in this assay. 25. Azilsartan medoxomil, azilsartan, and M-II were devoid of genotoxic potential in the Ames reverse mutation assay, in vitro Chinese Hamster Ovary Cell forward mutation assay, in vitro mouse lymphoma (tk) gene mutation test, ex vivo unscheduled DNA synthesis test, and in vivo mouse and/or rat bone marrow micronucleus assay. 26. Azilsartan medoxomil had no effect on the fertility of male or female rats at oral doses up to 1000 mg/kg/day. Fertility was also unaffected at doses up to 3000 mg/kg/day of M-II. 27. The safety profiles of azilsartan medoxomil and chlorthalidone monotherapy have been individually established. Pharmacologically-mediated toxicity, including suppression of body weight gain and decreased food consumption, was observed.
